name: brand
title: Brand
description: What the brand stands for: its promise, whom it speaks to, what sets it apart, and how it sounds.

files.brand.yaml:
unoverse: "1.0"
# The org's brand document (docs/unoverse/data/objects/elements/brand.md). The document in the pack
# (design/<org>/identity/brand.yaml) is the truth; this row is its presence, positioned like
# everything else so an agent finds it the way it finds a product. One per org: uniqueBy says so.
# A document has no call to action, so it embeds on five of the base's six.
type: object
name: brand
element: brand
# THE GLYPH its rows are drawn with (README 4a): a lucide icon name.
icon: palette
# NEVER A ROW (owner, 2026-09-14): the shape of an identity document, like organisation. An
# agent reads it through {{identity.<document>}} and the prompt blocks, never by search, so it
# extends nothing and declares no embed: it has no place on the map.

# THE FACE, as a node's node.yaml carries it: what this is and when an Agent reaches for it.
title: Brand
description: >-
  What the brand stands for: its promise, whom it speaks to, what sets it apart, and how it
  sounds.
whenToUse: >-
  Answer what the brand stands for, what to expect from it, whom it is for and what sets it
  apart; name the brands inside it; and give any writing its voice, the rules it follows and
  sentences in its own words. How it presents and how it sounds: the promise it makes and
  the words it makes it in.
category: Identity
version: 1.0.0

props: { $include: props }
files.props.yaml:
# THE BRAND DOCUMENT'S OWN FIELDS: every brief is the writer's instruction; the org's answers live in its pack.
name:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    The brand name as the enterprise presents it, which may differ from its trading name
    (a bank's card brand, a group's consumer brand). The site's logo text or title, not
    the legal entity.
  maxLength: 80
standsFor:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    What the name stands for, in one sentence, in the enterprise's own words where it says
    so (a tagline, a strapline, the meaning of the name, a 'who we are' line). Empty when
    it does not say.
  maxLength: 300
promise:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    The expectation the brand sets: what people can expect from it, in one or two
    sentences, drawn from the promises the site repeats on its home, about and brand
    pages. Written to the customer.
  maxLength: 400
represents:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    How the brand carries the purpose (read purpose.yaml first): in one paragraph, how the
    name, the promise and the way it presents itself express why the enterprise exists. In
    the enterprise's own words where it connects the two; empty when it does not.
  maxLength: 500
positioning:
  type: string
  input: true
  description: >-
    Whom the brand speaks to and how it wants to be seen by them, in one or two sentences,
    from the way the site addresses its customers and describes its position. Never
    invented segments.
  maxLength: 400
differentiators:
  type: array
  input: true
  description: >-
    What the enterprise claims sets its brand apart, three to six items, each in its own
    words (a first, a leadership claim, a partnership, a heritage). Only claims it makes
    itself.
  maxItems: 6
  items:
    type: string
brands:
  type: array
  input: true
  description: >-
    The brand tree: the sub-brands and product brands the enterprise presents under this
    brand (a card family, an app, a loyalty programme, a subsidiary), one entry per brand
    with its name as written and one sentence on what it is for, nested in `brands` where
    the enterprise nests them. Empty when it presents none; never invented.
  maxItems: 20
  items:
    name:
      type: string
      description: >-
        The name as the organisation writes it.
      maxLength: 80
    what:
      type: string
      description: >-
        One sentence, in the organisation's words.
      maxLength: 240
    brands:
      type: array
      description: >-
        The nested brands, in the same shape, where the organisation nests them.
rules:
  type: array
  input: true
  description: >-
    Three to six rules the site's copy visibly follows, each as 'Do this' or 'Never that':
    the person it addresses (you, we), its register (plain, formal, warm), sentence
    length, what it capitalises, what it never says.
  maxItems: 6
  items:
    type: string
examples:
  type: array
  input: true
  description: >-
    Three to five sentences copied verbatim from the site that show the voice. Quotes,
    never paraphrase.
  maxItems: 5
  items:
    type: string
whenToUse:
  type: string
  input: false
  description: >-
    When an agent should reach for this document, from the side of whoever is asking. Assigned from
    the object's manifest.
